keyVerseText: For as in the days that were before the flood they were eating and drinking, marrying and giving in marriage, until the day that Noe entered into the ark,
rootMeaning: The Greek preposition ἄχρι (áchri) is etymologically connected to ἄκρον (ákron), meaning 'one end' or 'extremity.' This root conveys the idea of a boundary or limit, emphasizing a point up to which something extends. Unlike the simple English glosses such as 'until' or 'till,' the root sense highlights a terminus or an utmost point in time, space, or degree, underscoring a definitive boundary rather than an indefinite duration.
usageInScripture: With 49 occurrences in the New Testament and related literature, ἄχρι is predominantly translated as 'until' (14 times), 'unto' (11 times), and 'till' (7 times), reflecting its primary function as a marker of temporal or spatial limits. Its usage consistently denotes a boundary or an extent, whether in time—indicating the duration up to a certain moment—or in space—marking a physical limit. The variety of translations such as 'while,' 'for,' and 'as far as' further reveal its flexibility but always within the framework of reaching a defined endpoint.
theologicalSignificance: Understanding ἄχρι as a term denoting a definitive boundary enriches our grasp of biblical texts that speak about God's timing and purposes. It reminds believers that God's plans unfold within appointed limits and that divine promises and judgments have precise moments of fulfillment. This precision in language reflects the sovereignty and faithfulness of God, who governs history with exactness. Moreover, the concept of a terminus invites Christians to live expectantly and faithfully until the appointed time, trusting in God's perfect timing and control over all things.
keyVerseReflection: Matthew 24:38 describes life 'until the day that Noe entered into the ark,' using ἄχρι to mark the exact point before the flood's onset. This word emphasizes the normalcy and continuity of life up to that critical boundary, underscoring the suddenness and significance of the coming judgment. It calls readers to awareness that just as life continued 'until' that decisive moment, so too must they be vigilant for the fulfillment of God's future purposes.
